title.narrative: UNDP - Främjad resiliens genom integrerat angreppsätt i Somalia
UNDP - Promoting resilience through integrated approach in Somalia

description.narrative:
Overall objective The project aims to build the capacity of the Somali authorities in their efforts to promote sustainable and resilient development through targeted support in the areas of integrated water resource management, environmental governance, and disaster risk reduction (DRR). The project integrates a youth perspective and inclusion in all components.
Component 1 - Integrated Water Resource Management Within the integrated approach to promoting sustainable and resilient development in Somalia, the specific objective of the component will be to build targeted capacities, both at the individual and institutional levels, to promote integrated water resource management (IWRM) in Somalia. In doing so, Somali institutions and the officials will be equipped with enhanced skills, tools, and systems on IWRM that would promote effective decision making on water allocations and efficient utilization of water resources at all levels.
Component 2 - Environmental Governance The specific objective of the component will be to enhance the capacities of the Somali authorities, both at federal and state levels, to address the ecological challenges and priorities toward improved environmental governance in the country. In doing so, the Directorate of Environment and the Federal Member States (FMS) will be capacitated towards strengthened environmental management, effective monitoring, and assessment and raise awareness through environmental education and advocacy.
Component 3 - Disaster Risk Reduction The objective of this component is to strengthen Somali institutions at Federal and State levels and put in place capacities, systems, and tools to support the transition from a culture of reactive responses to the practice of comprehensive disaster risk management in Somalia. A government-wide, multi-hazards, and multi-stakeholders approach will be adopted to integrate DRR in the planning and programming, across sectors and levels, focusing on promoting resilience of the disaster vulnerable communities.

UNDP Somalia har ansökt om finansiering från Sida på 75 miljoner SEK för genomförandet av projektet "Promoting resilience through integrated approach to water, environment & disaster risk management in Somalia". Programmet stödjer både den federala regeringen och alla delstater (Somaliland, Puntland, Galmadug, Jubaland, SouthWest och Hishabelle) under perioden 2020–2022.
Insatsen syftar till att bygga upp kapacitet så att Somalias myndigheter kan arbeta för att främja en hållbar och resilient utveckling genom riktat stöd på områdena integrerad vattenresurshantering, miljöförvaltning samt katastrofriskhantering. Insatsen har tre huvudsakliga komponenter. Komponent 1: Ökad kapacitet inom integrerad vattenresurshantering; Komponent 2: Förbättrad miljöförvaltning; Komponent 3: Kapacitetsuppbyggande för katastrofriskhantering. UNDP Somalia kommer att genomföra insatsen tillsammans med den federala regeringen, Somalias delstater och lokala NGO:er.
Insatsens totala budget är 75 miljoner SEK och Sverige står för hela finansieringen.

UNDP Somalia has applied to Sida for funding of 75 Million SEK to carry out the “Promoting resilience through integrated approach to water, environment & disaster risk management in Somalia”. The program supports both the Federal Government and all the Member States (Somaliland, Puntland, Galmadug, Jubaland, SouthWest and Hishabelle) during the period 2020-2023.
The Intervention aims to build the capacity of the Somalia authorities in their efforts to promote sustainable and resilient development through targeted support in the areas of integrated water resource management, environmental governance, and disaster risk reduction. The intervention has three main components. Component 1: Enhanced capacities in Integrated Water Resources Management (IWRM), Component 2: Improved Environmental Governance, Component 3: Capacity building for disaster risk management.
UNDP Somalia will implement the intervention together with Federal Government, Federal Members States of Somalia and local NGOs. The intervention’s total budget is 75 Million SEK fully funded by Sweden, and UNDP has the overall responsibility of quality assurance and accountability of the programme

sector.narrative: Water sector policy and administrative management

title.narrative: 13067 - 2nd amendment to the agreement with UNDP
13067 - Decision on 2nd amendment to the agreement

description.narrative:
The contribution achieved significant results in strengthening Somalia's resilience to water scarcity, environmental degradation, climate change and disaster risks through an integrated approach to water management, environmental governance, DRR and youth engagement.
Implemented between November 2020 and March 2025 with nationwide coverage, the programme successfully delivered its planned activities despite operating in a highly challenging context characterised by insecurity, political transition, recurrent climate shocks and humanitarian crises. With a total budget of 87,8 MSEK and a delivery rate of 100 per cent, the programme demonstrated strong implementation capacity and effective coordination among UN agencies, government institutions and national stakeholders.
A key expected result was strengthened institutional capacity at federal and state levels. The programme contributed to a shift from fragmented and reactive approaches towards more coordinated, preventive and sustainable management of water resources, environmental challenges and disaster risks. Capacity development reached more than 1000 federal and state officials in water management, while hundreds of government representatives were trained in gender-responsive disaster risk reduction and environmental governance. These efforts strengthened the ability of government institutions to develop policies, coordinate across sectors and integrate resilience considerations into planning and decision-making.
One of the most notable achievements was the establishment of Somalia's first Master of Science programme in Integrated Water Resources Management at Somali National University. Thirty-five students graduated from the programme, including 30% women, creating a new generation of Somali water professionals with advanced technical expertise. The programme also supported the establishment of a Geospatial Unit within the Ministry of Energy and Water Resources, staffed by 20 trained specialists and equipped to provide data and analysis for evidence-based water resource planning. These investments are expected to provide long-term benefits beyond the lifetime of the project by strengthening national expertise and institutional ownership.
In the environmental sector, the contribution strengthened the policy and regulatory framework for environmental governance. Key achievements included the development and validation of National Environmental Quality Standards, support for implementation of the National Environmental Strategy and Action Plan, and the development of Somalia's first Integrated Solid Waste Management Strategy. The programme also strengthened environmental monitoring systems through GIS technology, research partnerships and capacity development within government institutions. Public awareness campaigns reached communities across the country and contributed to increased awareness of environmental protection, plastic waste management and sustainable resource use.
The programme also generated important results in disaster risk reduction. A particularly significant achievement was support to the development and institutionalisation of Somalia's first comprehensive and gender-responsive National Disaster Risk Reduction Plan. At local level, 15 municipalities and high-risk districts developed DRR plans and community disaster management structures. More than 220 disaster volunteers were trained to support preparedness, response and recovery efforts within their communities. The upgrading of the National Emergency Operations Centre and the roll-out of community-based early warning systems strengthened the country's capacity to anticipate and respond to disasters, contributing to a gradual transition from emergency response towards risk management and preparedness.
Youth engagement emerged as one of the programme's strongest achievements and can be considered both an expected and unexpected result. While youth participation was an intended objective, the extent to which young people became active contributors to climate and environmental governance exceeded expectations. The establishment of the Somalia Youth Climate Platform brought together more than 350 young leaders, approximately half of them women, and created a sustainable national mechanism for youth engagement on climate resilience, environmental sustainability and disaster preparedness. Youth representatives contributed to national climate policy processes, including Somalia's Nationally Determined Contributions, and represented Somalia in international forums such as COP27 and COP28. The platform also strengthened collaboration between youth organisations, government institutions and development partners.
An additional unexpected result was the high level of ownership demonstrated by government institutions and youth networks. Rather than relying primarily on external technical assistance, several government counterparts increasingly assumed leadership roles in coordinating policies, training activities and planning processes. Similarly, youth groups evolved from programme beneficiaries into recognised stakeholders contributing to national policy discussions and awareness-raising initiatives. This increased ownership provides a stronger foundation for sustainability than originally anticipated.
Overall, the contribution successfully delivered results at policy, institutional and community levels. It strengthened human capital, established enduring institutional structures, improved national frameworks for environmental governance and disaster risk reduction, and created meaningful opportunities for youth engagement. The programme therefore made an important contribution to Somalia's long-term resilience and capacity to manage climate and environmental risks in a more coordinated, sustainable and nationally owned manner.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
